id: title:charlesvien:read timeouts from the task profile

review.posthog_relevance: Allows profile-specific configuration of task inactivity and max run duration, potentially supporting tiered or user-specific task behavior.
review.reason: Adds profile-dependent parameters (profile_idle_minutes, profile_max_wake_minutes) to task execution and their respective checks, while the actual profile lookup and settings implementation are absent. This represents a substantive, bounded capability improvement: the execution path is ready to use profile-specific values, but the dependency on the profile lookup is not implemented
review.uncertainty: The tier cannot reach 3 because the profile lookup and settings implementation are missing; the tier cannot reach 1 because the execution and checks are already implemented. The benefit is contingent on the missing profile implementation.

observations.limitations: This chunk does not include the implementation of the profile lookup and the profile-related settings, only the changes to the inactivity and max run duration resolution and the tests. The tier cannot be established without seeing the profile implementation and the profile-related settings.

observations.behavior: Adds profile_idle_minutes and profile_max_wake_minutes parameters to resolve_inactivity_timeout and its callers, and adds profile_idle_minutes and profile_max_wake_minutes fields to TaskProcessingContext. P1.F1.H3 adds a check: if profile_idle_minutes is not None, return timedelta(minutes=profile_idle_minutes). P1.F4.H3 adds a check: if profile_max_wake_minutes is not None, return
observations.code_quote: if cap is None or self.profile_max_wake_minutes is None:
observations.posthog_connection: This could allow a profile to override the default inactivity and max run duration settings. This could help with tiered or profile-specific task behavior.
